FAR WIDE ICONIC MYTH INK STILL like ulbul-chang-walks emptiness plus Joseon sumi: 60–70% empty paper, figures SMALL, One Piece splash scale. WIDE. Paper-white grass. ONE DEVICE: a white horse kneeling, head down, to a single pale-gold egg on the mound — at most ONE translucent gold wash on the egg. Tiny HYUKGOSE not yet a boy, still the egg. Six tiny elder silhouettes at the far left edge, creeping up. Winged horse allowed as myth. Monumental emptiness. No text. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = hyukgose. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.
